question: If the government decides to privatise a major public sector industry, what might be an unintended consequence ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential monopolistic practices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the government decides to privatize a major public sector industry, there is a risk of creating **potential monopolistic practices**.
 
• Privatization often leads to the concentration of market power in the hands of a few private entities, which can result in **reduced competition**.
 
• This reduction in competition can allow privatized entities to **set higher prices** and reduce the quality of goods or services.
 
• Monopolistic practices can lead to **consumer exploitation** as there are fewer alternatives available in the market.
 
• The lack of competition may also reduce the incentive for the privatized industry to innovate or improve **efficiency** over time.
 
• Regulatory oversight becomes critical in preventing these practices, but it can be challenging and resource-intensive for the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reduction in corruption**__

 __
 
• Privatization can potentially lead to a **reduction in corruption** by minimizing bureaucratic red tape and inefficiencies.
 
• However, this is not always guaranteed, as private entities can also engage in corrupt practices.
 
 
 
• **Immediate increase in public revenue**__
 __
 
• Privatization often results in an **immediate influx of funds** for the government through the sale of assets.
 
• This is a short-term benefit and does not address long-term economic impacts.
 
 
 
• **Enhancement of operational efficiency**__
 
 
• Private companies typically aim for **higher efficiency** and profitability compared to public sector entities.
 
• This can lead to better management and improved operational practices.
